claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 can be synthesized by arc melting.
Slow cooling of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 produces a complex crystalline or multiphase microstructure.
Melt-spinning can rapidly quench the alloy at approximately 10^5 to 10^6 K/s.
Rapid quenching at 10^5 to 10^6 K/s improves glass-forming ability relative to slow cooling.
Rapid quenching at 10^5 to 10^6 K/s improves the thermal stability of the amorphous state relative to slow cooling.
Rapid cooling suppresses the nucleation and growth of crystalline phases.
Rapid cooling kinetically freezes a disordered atomic arrangement.
Rapid quenching minimizes atomic diffusion during solidification.
Minimizing atomic diffusion inhibits the formation of equilibrium crystalline phases.
Phosphorus and high mixing entropy enhance glass-forming ability in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Phosphorus and high mixing entropy lower the free-energy barrier for amorphous-state formation.
The combined effects of phosphorus and high mixing entropy enhance the thermal stability of the resulting glass.
Rapidly quenched Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has an amorphous structure.
The rapidly quenched material will be fully amorphous, as indicated by the absence of crystalline XRD peaks.
Rapidly quenched samples will have a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature than samples cooled at approximately 52 K/s.
Cooling at approximately 52 K/s produces a complex crystalline microstructure in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Samples cooled at approximately 52 K/s have lower amorphous-state thermal stability than rapidly quenched samples.
Cooling rates below the rapid-quenching range may be insufficient to prevent crystallization.
The intervention should apply broadly to phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys when composition and other processing parameters are controlled.
Substantial composition changes, nonuniform cooling, quench-induced stresses, or local inhomogeneities may limit the intervention's effectiveness or reproducibility.
